articleTitle: A Proposal of Python Programming Exercise Problems for Basic Statistics Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Statistical learning with programming can be used to improve statistical literacy, teach students, and promote educational innovations in information-driven universities through technology-mediated statistical course. However, many novice students struggle with studying it due to the complexities involved in learning statistics through programming. In this works, we propose a study of Python programming exercise problems focusing on the Element Fill-in-Blank Problem (EFP), Grammar-concept Understanding Problem (GUP), and ValueTrace Problem (VTP) as a tools for self-studying statistics. String matching methods were implemented to analyze and verify the proper solution in the each responses. For the evaluations, we generated 14 instances problem for introduction to statistics study, then assigned them to 67 first-year undergraduate students in UPN “Veteran” Jawa Timur, Indonesia. The empirical results proved that the proposed study is applicable for helping student to learn statistics using Python programming approach.

articleTitle: Design and Development UI/UX on Simulation of Earthquake Mitigation Based Mobile Virtual Reality
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: This research delves into the design and development of User Interface (UI) and User Experience (UX) for a mobile virtual reality (VR) application aimed at simulating earthquake mitigation strategies. Earthquakes pose significant threats to communities worldwide, necessitating innovative approaches for preparedness and mitigation. Leveraging the immersive capabilities of VR technology, this study focuses on creating a realistic simulation environment that enables users to experience and learn about effective mitigation techniques. Through an iterative design process, incorporating principles of UI/UX design, human-computer interaction, and disaster management, the research aims to enhance user engagement, comprehension, and retention of earthquake mitigation practices. The study also explores the integration of interactive elements, feedback mechanisms, and educational content within the VR environment to promote effective learning and decision-making during simulated earthquake scenarios. This study shows System Usability Scale (SUS) score is 72.475, this result make the design of this simulation can use in average user.

articleTitle: Internet-Based Road Air Quality Monitoring System
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: This research introduces the development of a road air quality monitoring system, where the measurement data is integrated into a web server via an internet connection. Air quality has become a significant concern in urban areas due to the rise in air pollution. Jakarta serves as an example of a city grappling with this issue. The high volume of vehicles on Jakarta’s roads leads to elevated air pollution levels from exhaust emissions. Monitoring road air quality is crucial for health and safety reasons. This monitoring needs to be conducted at various locations along the road. Each location’s measurement is performed using a measurement unit, with the data from all units being integrated. In this study, a prototype of the measurement unit is developed. It is constructed using the NodeMCU ESP32 microcontroller and two air quality sensors, MQ-7 and MQ-135, to measure the concentrations of carbon monoxide (CO) and carbon dioxide (CO<inf xmlns:mml="http://www.w3.org/1998/Math/MathML" xmlns:xlink="http://www.w3.org/1999/xlink">2</inf>), respectively. The NodeMCU ESP32 processes and transmits the measurement data to a web server, ensuring the data is integrated into a server. Experimental test results demonstrated that the prototype could measure air quality, store the data on a server, and present real-time measurement data in a web application.

articleTitle: Effect of Bit Transmission Amount on Wireless Sensor Networks on Estx Optimum and Minimum ESB
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: In Wireless Sensor Networks, energy efficiency is a very critical issue because sensor nodes have limited battery resources. The relationship between the number of transmitted bits, Estx, and ESB, a more energy-efficient communication protocol can be designed, thereby extending the lifetime of the sensor network. This study uses approaches with the Nelder Mead Simplex method. This study to estimate Estx and ESB based on the number of transmitted bits. The study was conducted using sensor nodes to measure the energy used in transmission and standby mode. The obtained data were analyzed using certain statistical techniques to evaluate the relationship between the number of bits, Estx, and ESB. The results show that the number of transmitted bits has a significant effect on Estx and ESB. It is found that the optimal Estx and minimum ESB can be achieved by adjusting the number of transmitted bits, which has implications for reducing the total energy consumption in the network. In addition, a linear relationship between the number of bits and Estx can be found, while ESB can be minimized with appropriate energy saving strategies. This study makes an important contribution to the field of Wireless Sensor Networks by offering practical guidance for designing more energy-efficient communication protocols. The findings in this study show that the best modulation to determine the optimum Estx and minimum ESB is 16 QAM modulation. In addition, the use of the best modulation can be used to determine the optimum Estx and minimum ESB values influenced by the number of bits. These findings are expected to improve operational efficiency and extend the life of wireless sensor networks, supporting various WSN applications more effectively.

articleTitle: The Effect of Academic Engagement and Self-Efficacy on Digital Literacy Learning Achievement
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Academic engagement and self-efficacy are two traits that contribute to the success of student’s learning process. Prior studies are only limited on examining academic engagement during offline learning mode. The present study aims to reveal how academic engagement and self-efficacy affected students’ learning achievements in Digital Literacy class. There were three variables examined in this study covering academic engagement, self-efficacy, and learning achievements. Academic engagement referred to students’ participation in learning activities included asking questions and taking part in online discussion. There were 143 students enrolled in a Digital Literacy class involved as the participants. Data were collected using a questionnaire using a four-point Likert’s scaling method. The obtained data were analyzed using multiple linear regression by the assistance of SPSS software. The findings demonstrated that academic engagement and self-efficacy significantly affected students’ digital literacy learning achievements for about 81.8%, while the rest of $\mathbf{1 8. 2 \%}$ was influenced by other traits.

articleTitle: Left Ventricular Wall Segmentation Using U-Net and Link-Net
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Myocardial Infarction (MI) is categorized as the world’s deadliest illnesses. It can be identified by looking for anomalies in the left ventricular wall through the heart ultrasound imaging method. Unfortunately, these types of images are often of poor quality, making it difficult for paramedics to identify them. Segmentation of the left ventricular wall in cardiac ultrasound images will be carried out to aid paramedics in seeing the left ventricular wall more clearly. U-Net architecture and its extension, Link-Net architecture, are employed in this study to do this segmentation. Both architectures share the use of skip-connections to enhance spatial information. The publicly available data from Tampere University, Qatar University, and Hamad Medical Corporation (HMC-QU) is chosen to demonstrate the work of these two architectures in segmenting the left ventricular wall. The results of the training indicate that Link-Net has a 13% faster training time when compared to U-Net. The highest training and validation accuracies achieved by Link-Net are 0.9973 and 0.9941. Link-Net is also superior by obtaining the highest F1 Score of 0.9636 throughout the testing phase. Both architectures have proven effective segmenting the left ventricular wall. The findings of this study have been shown to facilitate and improve the accuracy of medical practitioners in diagnosing MI.

articleTitle: Design and Analysis of A Plastic Optical Fiber Network for Automobile Braking System
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Polymeric optical fiber (POF) is a flexible and transparent plastic fiber used in various applications, including for a sensing system in automobile brake systems. This research study proposed the design and analysis of a plastic optical fiber network for automobile brake systems. The method is to utilize the light emitted from the vehicle’s backlight, which is then captured by the brake system detector. The design employs an optical communication system because of its advantageous features, such as high-speed data transmission and communication reliability. The power budget of the link is analyzed through theoretical calculations and simulations. The proposed system can achieve a Q factor of 8.29 and a power margin of 11.26 dB. This condition indicates that the proposed design can function properly in terms of data transmission and sufficient transmitted power.

articleTitle: Analysis of the Use of E-Learning Web/Applications among Students During Pandemic
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: This research explores E-learning of Bina Nusantara University that was used on the pandemic era that changes from face-to-face learning to E-learning because of the outspread of Covid-19 that forces learning systems to changes drastically. This research uses the Structural Equation Model (SEM) to make sure that E-learning is effective in the pandemic era and can be used until the post-pandemic era. Data collected from 111 respondents through survey that shows the respondents ever experience E-learning that Bina Nusantara University used during the pandemic era and active students until the post-pandemic era. Analysis of the data using SmartPLS 4.0 Tools validated the research model. These findings spotlight the use of E-learning during the pandemic and will E-learning be useful, effective, reliable, and comfortable during the post-pandemic era. There are 8 hypotheses found, with 7 accepted and 1 rejected.

articleTitle: Stability Analysis of Transfer Switch Process between Solar Power Plant and Grid Source
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: In this research discusses the stability of the transfer switch process in the automatic transfer switch between solar power plant and grid source. The ATS used is ATS with semiconductor switching components in this case using triac controlled by ESP 8266 microcontroller with opto isolator triac driver MOC 3063 which has been equipped with zero crossing circuit. From the ATS circuit that has been made, testing and stability analysis is carried out during the transfer switch process. Indicators of stability are seen from transient events, oscillations, and fluctuations. Tests were carried out using three different loads, namely resistive loads, inductive loads, and capacitive loads. Each type of load was tested 5 times grid source to solar power plant source and 5 times solar power plant source to grid source. The test results show that the switch transfer process runs quite well and is stable. No electrical instability events were found that could have a negative impact on the electricity system. There was only a slight increase in peak voltage in the first wave after switching. The increase is still relatively safe because the value does not exceed 5% in accordance with the general regulations for electrical installations 2000. In the transfer switch process, there is a momentary power outage because there is a delay set for 200ms. With this delay, the time lag between the death of the first source and the life of the second source ranges from 160ms to 180.5ms.

articleTitle: Model Free Predictive Current Control Based on Sliding Mode Observer for BLDC Motor Drive
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Brushless DC Motor (BLDCM) has become popular for electric drive system due to the advantages compared to brushed DC Motor. Nevertheless, it requires a more complex control system to achieve better performance. Model Predictive Control (MPC) offers improvements in the BLDC drive system. However, model and parameter uncertainties can deteriorate the MPC because of incorrect prediction of the model. This paper proposes Model Free Predictive Control (MFPC) for BLDC drives with Ultra Local Model (ULM) approach. ULM’s unknown parts are estimated using Sliding Mode Observer (SMO) to predict the BLDC currents required in the MPC. This paper aims to design the proposed control and investigate the performance in BLDC drive and compare it to traditional MPC in handling parameter uncertainty. The result shows that with proper SMO gain, the MFPCSMO achieved fast dynamic response with lower ripples and steady state errors for both speed and torque performance compared to traditional FCSMPC. In addition, the proposed method is completely independent of BLDCM model as well as motor parameter and produces excellent performance in parameter mismatch conditions with lower ripples.

articleTitle: Design an optimal FOPD controller for electric vehicle speed tracking control
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Electric Vehicles (EVs) become very important issue and gained attention due to many reasons like its economic price, saving environment and more reliable. In this study, controlling speed for EV is utilized by tracking the desired speed using Fractional Order Proportional Derivative (FOPD) controller with a smart tuning algorithm named Sunflower Optimization (SFO) algorithm to satisfy robust and efficient controlled speed. The numerical analysis is obtained using Matlab program in two steps, controlling the system to reach the desired value in best and stable response then apply two undesired signals (disturbance signals) to test system robustness and finally compare the suggested controller with different conventional controllers(Normal PD controller-Optimal PD controller).

articleTitle: Challenges in Engineering Education: Addressing Language Barriers, Time Management Issues, and Mental Health Concerns
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Language barriers, time management issues, and mental health issues are the main issues that define studying difficulties among engineering students. This paper is conducted to answer this investigation on the sampled students of an engineering college at a public university. The results reveal that 53% of students possess only moderate English skills, contributing to comprehension difficulties in lectures for over half the cohort. Additionally, nearly 38% of students struggle with missing key information, indicating that challenges are not merely linguistic but also pertain to content delivery. Time management is another critical issue, with a significant proportion of students admitting to average skills and habitual procrastination, culminating in a prevalent trend of last-minute studying that exacerbates stress. The mental health of students is alarmingly compromised, with nearly 70% reporting physical symptoms due to academic pressure and a majority grappling with restlessness and mood fluctuations. These findings underscore the urgent need for educational institutions to prioritize student support services and mental health resources. Implementing strategies to address these challenges can greatly improve the overall well-being and academic success of students.

articleTitle: The Effect of Batch Size, Shape, and Filter on CNN Architecture for the Classification of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia Using Colposcopy Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Colposcopy is a medical procedure that provides detailed visualization of the cervix and is non-invasive for the patient. Junior colposcopists only have sensitivity (55-64%) when performing colposcopic examination to determine the category of Cervical Intraepithelial Neoplasia (CIN) in patients. In addition, the accuracy of colposcopy examination result is essential for doctors’ decision-making in treating patients. Currently, numerous studies support decision-making in CIN using artificial intelligence. Existing research predominantly employs pre-trained transfer learning models, such as “imagenet”, which are trained on many images rather than specific CIN images. Therefore, this study proposes a classification approach that leverages pre-trained models on specific CIN images, utilizing a base Convolutional Neural Network (CNN) method. The parameters of the CNN are optimized by fine-tuning the filter kernel. The accuracy performance of the testing stage improved to 0.83, and the sensitivity increased to 0.84. The primary strategy is to combine the filter kernel parameters of the base CNN in the training stage, tuning the shape of filter kernel parameters to [128,64,32]. The first filter kernel is $5 \times 5$ and the second and third filter kernels are $3 \times 3$, resulting in a training accuracy performance of 0.83, validation accuracy of 0.61, and training time requirement of 66.28 minutes using Apple M1 Chip. In the future, a basic CNN will be developed using CIN data with green filters to create a model specifically used for the supervised identification of CIN characteristics.

articleTitle: Road Damage Classification Based on Second Order Features Using Random Forest
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Roads are essential infrastructure; therefore, regular maintenance is vital. Classification of road damage is a necessary step in automatic road. Manually classifying road damage can be time-consuming and may introduce uncertainty due to the subjective nature of the officer’s evaluation of road conditions. Various machine learning strategies, such as decision trees, KNN, and SVM, are employed to automate the categorization of road damage. The study presents a method that depends on the Random Forest (RF) algorithm for classifying road damage, supported by second-order feature extraction. The selection of this technique for extracting the second-order feature is based on its ability to capture the interrelationships among piksel, provide more detailed information about the image, and provide various textual characteristics that aid in a more comprehensive and extensive analysis. The study also compared the accuracy of various machine-learning systems. The experiment findings demonstrated that the Random Forest method exceeded other strategies by achieving an accuracy rate of $\mathbf{9 9 \%}$. At the same time, SVM, KNN, and Decision Tree had an accuracy value of $\mathbf{9 6. 3 3 \%}, \mathbf{9 8. 3 3 \%}$, and $\mathbf{9 8 \%}$. The Random Forest algorithm’s high accuracy is due to its ensemble approach, which enhances generalization and reduces overfitting, rendering it a superior choice for complex classification tasks in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Medication Reminder and Tracker Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Medication adherence is a critical concern for persons suffering from chronic illnesses. People may struggle to remember to take their prescriptions on time, especially if they have a hectic schedule or are traveling. Developing and providing a reliable application can help those in need to remind individuals to take their respective medicine. A Medication Reminder and Tracker Application addresses these problems as one of the main reasons for developing this system. This is an Android-based application which users can install either on or between these operating systems. Users can manually enter their medication, the recommended dosage, and the appropriate time to take it. This program provides related healthcare advice and tips that users can read through the system’s various descriptions of ailments. It uses a good user interface that is easy to navigate for individuals.

articleTitle: Analysis Of The Level Of Thinking On Vocational High School Students 1 Jabon Sidoarjo Using Rasch Modeling
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: In the era of Industrial Revolution 4.0, technological advances have brought significant changes in various aspects of life, including education. Assessment management in Vocational High Schools (SMK) is critical to measure students’ level of thinking. Rasch modeling allows analysis of student learning outcomes to assess their critical and analytical thinking abilities. The results of this research are expected to provide insight into the distribution of students’ levels of thinking and provide recommendations for more comprehensive and fair assessment methods. The method used was one group pre-test post-test, which was applied to 30 students at Vocational High School 1 Jabon Sidoarjo. The reliability in Cronbach alpha was found to be 0.82, which means the questions were in an outstanding category. Some students answered questions by guessing. It is recommended that interactive PowerPoint media be used under ten pages so that the learning process can be effective and get feedback.

articleTitle: Investigations of Proper Video Games in Handgrip Exergame System for Hypertension Prevention
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Currently, hypertension is a major health concern. It is affecting approximately 1.28 billion people around the world due to the World Health Organization (WHO). Handgrip exercises performed with a foam ball have proven to be an effective approach to lowering blood pressure. To promote such exercises in a fun and engaging way, we have developed a handgrip exergame system to play video games with various hand gestures on a personal computer equipped with a camera. A Python program is implemented with Mediapipe to detect hand gestures to control games. Then, the selection of proper games is essential for easy use by seniors. In this paper, we investigate video games using two or four hand gestures for the handgrip exergame system through applications to 10 Indonesian seniors who are suffering from hypertension. We asked them to play the nine video games in the system and to answer to $\mathbf{1 0}$ questions on the usability. The System Usability Scale (SUS) score of the questionnaire results validated the effectiveness of the proposal.

articleTitle: Hardware Accelerator for CNN using Optimized Multiply Accumulate Structure
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Convolution is a critical operation in FPGA-based hardware accelerators, yet existing designs often overlook FPGA’s inherent architecture, posing challenges for hardware resource efficiency. Despite previous attempts with approximate multipliers and convolution acceleration algorithms, accuracy loss and resource occupation lead to performance degradation. This work proposes resource efficient optimized accurate multipliers based on LUTs and carry chains for FPGA platforms. A generic multiply-accumulate structure is constructed, directly accumulating partial products from optimized radix-4 Booth multipliers, demonstrating a maximum $51 \%$ LUT reduction compared to Vivado area-optimized multipliers. The convolutional process unit achieves a ${3 6 \%}$ LUT reduction. This Multiply Accumulate (MAC) structure with distributed arithmetic achieves greater reduction in delay and high-speed operation. Implementation details include critical path delay, power, and resource usage calculations are done using Cadence software and Virtex 7 FPGA board in Xilinx Vivado 2021.2. The inherent advantages of using ASIC for development and its trade-offs are also discussed. Implementation details include the parameters like power, area, delay and data path of the main module used to classify the 28X28 pixel grayscale digits (0-9) in MNIST dataset using Recurrent Convolutional Neural Networks (CNN). The circuit is synthesized using Cadence Genus to obtain the schematic and its associated resource values, timing, power and area reports. The logic verification and output waveforms are obtained using Cadence Incisive Simulator.

articleTitle: Design and Evaluation of On-Grid Solar Rooftop Power Plant for Tower I of Ministry 3 Building in the New Indonesian Capital City
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: The increasing need for electrical energy has encouraged the Government of Indonesia to develop renewable energy, including rooftop solar power plants (SPP) as part of the strategy to achieve a $23 \%$ renewable energy mix by 2025. This study aims to design and evaluate an on-grid rooftop PV system for Tower 1 of Kemenko Building 3 in the New Capital City of Indonesia. This system is expected to support the green building concept and contribute to the Net Zero Emission target. Using PVsyst 7.2 software and weather data from Meteonorm 8.0 (Pvsyst database), simulations were conducted to determine the optimal configuration for solar energy production. The research location is at coordinates $0.9638^{\circ} \mathrm{S}$, and $116.6985^{\circ} \mathrm{E}$ with a roof area of $875 \mathrm{~m}^{2}$. After being simulated using PVsyst, the optimal configuration for annual energy production was obtained at 67.3 MWh with a solar panel tilt angle of 10° and an azimuth of 0° (facing north). The SPP system is designed using 550 WP monocrystalline modules arranged in 5 strings with 16 modules in each string, as well as an inverter from Canadian Solar with a capacity of 40 kW. Technical analysis also recorded a performance ratio (PR) of 0.835, indicating an operational efficiency of around $83.5 \%$ of ideal conditions. The proposed SPP configuration is capable of producing optimal energy and supporting the development of renewable energy in new urban areas. Implementing of this rooftop SPP is also an important step in helping the sustainable development plan in the New Capital City of Indonesia.

articleTitle: Design of Forward DC-DC Converter for SCC using Cascaded Controller
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: In this paper presented design of forward DC-DC converter for solar charging controller (SCC) implementation in renewable energy systems. It aims to optimize energy conversion efficiency and to enhance the performances. The renewable energy has recently become a prominent topic due environmentally friendly energy, as well as its advanced technology. The implementation of forward DC-DC converter as solar charging controller (SCC) is essential for regulating battery parameters and managing power flow from photovoltaic (PV) to battery. In addition, a cascaded proportional-integral (PI) controller is utilized to manage current and voltage parameters, thereby preventing battery overcharging. Control parameters are determined using the Ziegler-Nichols method reaction curve based. This method is used to obtained the precise control parameters. A MATLAB software is used for simulation and controller design State of charge (SoC) variations are presented in two scenarios: with and without the controller. The SoC levels are set at ${2 5 \%}, {5 0 \%}$ and ${9 5 \%}$, where a high SoC percentage indicates a nearly full battery capacity, and a low SoC percentage indicates a nearly empty battery capacity. With the cascaded controller, both current and voltage responses across different SoC levels demonstrate satisfactory performance, including rapid transient responses, minimal overshoot, small ripples, and robustness.

articleTitle: IoT-based Billiard Table Management System
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: In the digital era, Internet of Things (IoT) technology has transformed the operation of various industries, including the entertainment industry. IoT enables devices to connect and communicate over the internet. This study develops an IoT-based billiard table usage management system to improve operational efficiency in billiard cafes. This system uses the Raspberry Pi Pico W and the MQTT protocol to control and monitor billiard table lights in real-time, ensuring accurate time management and billing. The system is tested to ensure response time and performance. The test results show that this system functions well over long periods, can handle high number of requests, and updates billing status in real-time. The developed mobile application allows efficient monitoring and management of billiard table usage with features such as billing system and revenue analytics. The integration of IoT in billiard table management demonstrates significant improvements in operational efficiency and billing accuracy, making it an effective and innovative solution for entertainment businesses. This approach also provides a strong foundation for further development and adoption of IoT technology in other sectors requiring efficient operational management.

articleTitle: Educational Training on Business Management Using Web-Based Applications with Cryptocurrency Integration
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: The business model has developed significantly in various aspects and fields. One of the most popular models is the Business Model Canvas, which has greatly helped people build their businesses. With advancements in technology, this model has been combined with artificial intelligence (AI) into a web-based application. Moreover, we have integrated cryptocurrency into our application to provide players with a real-time business environment experience. Additionally, we have developed both administrator and player systems, which are user-friendly and adaptable to various languages. Based on the experimental results, anyone who has played this simulation/training has done so without any problems. The team with the highest Net Profit Value (NPV) is nominated as the winner in this business simulation/training. Our demo can be accessed at https://mbs.topboss.com/demo.

articleTitle: Voltage Control of DC Microgrid using Arctic Puffin Optimization Algorithm for Tuning of Sliding Mode Control Gain
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: In general, voltage control is an important issue in terms of system stability and reliability especially when the penetration level of renewable units increases with potential a role for DC microgrids. Sliding Mode Control (SMC) is known widely for its insensitivity to system uncertainties and external disturbances, but it highly relies on the exactness of tuning control gains. In this paper, the Arctic Puffin Optimization (APO) algorithm is employed to obtain optimal tuning of SMC gains for improved voltage control in DC microgrids. Inspired by the Arctic Puffins behavior, APO algorithm proposed a new way to balance exploration and exploitation in search space hence it is suitable to solve challenging optimization problems. Comprehensive simulations and comparative analysis have established that the proposed APO-tuned SMC will improve voltage control performance with much less managing effort and with better system stability regardless of the running situations. In the presented results, the paper explicitly showed that SMC tuned by APO for voltage control has a good performance.

articleTitle: Analysis of Surface Wave Control on Enhanced Circular Microstrip Antennas for 5G Applications
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: The introduction of 5G technology involves enhanced antenna designs to meet the demands for increased data rates and better performance. This research provides a complete investigation of how Electromagnetic Band-Gap (EBG) structures affect the performance of microstrip antennas designed for 5 G applications. Besides, the surface wave determination in two and three dimensions was explained. EBG structures are used to reduce surface wave propagation, which has been shown to drawback antenna performance by producing undesired radiation patterns and diminishing efficiency. Through extensive simulations using CST microwave studio, this work proves that embedding EBG in circular microstrip antennas reduces antenna size by 3. 97%. Furthermore, the processes for determining surface current in the selected places were detailed in-depth

articleTitle: An Introduction of Test Code Approach in Basic Java Programming Course
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Students and teachers in Computer Science field have considered Java as an essential programming language to learn for many years. To support activities of teachers and students in programming learning, a web-based system has been developed called the Java Programming Learning Assistant System (JPLAS). Code Writing Problem (CWP) is one of the exercise problems in JPLAS. It verifies student answer codes using test codes by running them on JUnit. Currently, most teachers manually verify answer codes, which may cause errors, slow feedback, and differences in assessment standards between teachers. In this paper, we present a test code approach for assignments in an existing basic Java programming course. For evaluations, we made test codes for some assignments in the basic Java programming course at Malang State Polytechnic, Indonesia, and applied them to existing student answer codes. The results confirm both the efficacy and validity.

articleTitle: Analysis of New Cascade Multilevel Inverter Topology on Harmonic Distortion And Power Efficiency of Single-Phase Electrical Power
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Multilevel inverter (MLI) have advanced significantly, particularly in renewable energy systems like Solar Power Plants (PLTS), which produce Direct Current (DC). Previous studies have shown that inverters generating 11level waveforms require many MOSFET components, increasing production costs and leading to high Total Harmonic Distortion (THD) due to the complexity of switching methods. This study proposes a solution by developing a New Cascade Multilevel Inverter topology that uses only 8 MOSFETs to generate an 11-level waveform, reducing the number of components and simplifying the switching method. The research contribution lies in offering a novel inverter topology that improves efficiency with fewer components, enhances modularity, and maintains high power performance. The methodology involves using MATLAB Simulink for simulation, with the designed topology and Selective Harmonic Elimination Pulse Width Modulation (SHEPWM) as the switching method, controlled by a Pulse Generator within the simulation. The results indicate that this new inverter topology achieves a THD value of 3.59% across all load types (resistive, resistive-inductive, and resistive-capacitive) and a power efficiency of $\mathbf{9 9. 8 5 \%}$, calculated by comparing the input and output currents of the inverter connected to the load. this study analyzes a new inverter topology capable of producing an 11-level waveform using only 8 MOSFETs, achieving a THD value of $\mathbf{3. 5 9 \%}$, and a power efficiency of $\mathbf{9 9. 8 5 \%}$, tested with three different load combinations.

articleTitle: Feature Extraction and Preprocessing Techniques on Open-Ended Concept Mapping Activity Log Data
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Concept maps are graphic representations of unique ideas widely used in learning. Concept mapping activities are often stored in an activity log which contains a record of data based on a particular time. The high activity of concept mapping can form extensive data collection and result in abundant information. An appropriate initial processing action is needed to process the concept mapping log data properly. This study aims to reduce the concept of map activity log data to obtain a reliable and noise-free dataset. This research begins with the data preprocessing stage, the initial technique in data mining that converts raw data into cleaner information and can be used for further processing. The preprocessing phase could be done using the data reduction method or adding a filter example to observe missing data on an attribute by eliminating missing observation data. The principal component analysis algorithm was used to normalize the data to become stable, neither too high nor too low. This study emphasizes that the extracted data could produce high accuracy and shorter processing time.

articleTitle: Probabilistic-based Text Clustering for Optimizing Mental Health Issues Extraction on Social Media
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: This study investigated mental health issues in the context of conversations on the social media platform Twitter. Data was collected over the last three years with the keywords mental health, suicide, and depression. The research method uses text mining with the Latent Dirichlet Allocation model. The results of the analysis have been able to identify 8 main topics based on high coherence scores. The dominant topic found on social media Twitter is about religious (20%) and social perspectives on suicide (14,7%). These findings indicate that Twitter conversations often reflect debate and reflection on how religious values and social views affect the perception and treatment of mental health problems, especially suicide. The study provides in-depth insights into the dynamics of online conversations around mental health on social media, highlighting the complexity of the interaction between religious, social, and mental health factors in a digital context. The implications of this study can be used as a basis for the development of more sensitive and effective intervention strategies and communication approaches in overcoming stigmatization and increasing public understanding of mental health issues, especially those related to suicide. The validation of the LDA model for the topic instruction task showed an interpretation accuracy of 83% for word tasks and 87% for topic tasks. This suggests that the LDA model is highly effective in identifying mental health issues, with an accuracy exceeding 80% when aligned with respondents’ views.

articleTitle: A Novel Method Implemented for Deadlock Problems in FMSs Modeled with Petri Nets
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: A novel method implemented for deadlock problems is specified to perfectly liveness, which is crucial to Petri Net(PN) models. In this article, we apply four classes of PN execution to models of complex Flexible Manufacturing Systems (FMSs) environments. The significant paradigm presented for S4PR-net is characterized by high efficiency in the distribution of modeling complex interactive FMSs. We formulate this problem as a complete multi-resource production system using advanced automation technologies in response to it. The optimal reconfigurable FMS is implemented by designing the controller transitions (CTs) in the PNs models, and this approach eliminates all deadlock statuses. The methodology and models developed can be used CTs are provided effectively for PNs when adding the recapture transitions usually associated with deadlock (DL)-free, which conserved all markings. More specifically, this framework permits PN’s Reachability Graphs (RG) to guarantee maximum permissive for FMS allowing multiple active resources. Several examples have been experimental results to demonstrate PNs that contain computer simulation models and are much more efficient. simulation models and are much more efficient.

articleTitle: Utilizing Usability Testing for User Interface Improvement: Case Study on Unesa’s Academic Mobile Application
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Surabaya State University (Unesa) utilizes modern information technology through an academic service system, Siakadu Mobile Application, to enhance efficiency and effectiveness in academic and administrative processes. Motivated by the application’s importance, this study evaluates users’ experiences completing academic activities and proposes visual improvements. Features such as uploading assignments and learning materials, checking similarity reports, and reminding assignment deadines are crucial to both lecturers and students; hence, they become this study’s main objects. This study then carries out a user-centric pipeline centred on users’ needs and feedback to improve users’ satisfaction and the application’s efficiency. Throughout the research process, evaluation processes, encompassing interviews, observations, and hands-on trials with users, provide valuable insights that guided the development of questionnaires targeting data visualization and application effectiveness. Upon completing the assessment and prototyping, our findings indicate significant improvements in user engagement and task management efficiency, underscoring the application’s impact on academic processes. These results further suggest that ongoing user feedback is crucial for continuous enhancement.

articleTitle: Gamification in Viat-Map Application to Improve Student’s Experiences and the Relation with Their Performance
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Gamification refers to the application of game-design elements and principles in non-game contexts to enhance user engagement and motivation. By incorporating elements such as points, badges, levels, avatars, and leaderboards, gamification seeks to make learning experiences more interactive and rewarding. This study examines the integration of gamification features within the Viat-Map application, which utilizes the Toulmin argumentation model to improve students’ comprehension of texts. The research involved 66 sophomore students from the State Polytechnic of Malang, divided into control and experimental groups. The experimental group used the Viat-Map application enhanced with gamification elements, while the control group used a version without these features. The study employed post-tests, and surveys to assess the impact of gamification on student engagement and performance. Results indicate that students using the gamified version of the application reported more positive learning experiences and demonstrated better academic performance compared to those using the non-gamified version. These findings highlight the potential of gamification to enrich educational applications, making learning more engaging and effective.

articleTitle: A Tree-Based Model for Predicting Student Achievement in Online Learning Environments
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: An important instrument of academic performance is student engagement in online learning. This work built a prediction model based on decision trees to find elements influencing student engagement in online learning settings. Examined were involvement, interaction, responsiveness to criticism, and academic performance. Examining the correlations between these factors and student involvement levels using decision trees revealed According to the findings, student involvement was highly predicted by participation and interaction; followed by responsiveness to criticism and academic performance. The approach reveals great accuracy in estimating engagement levels, which let teachers find children who may need certain interventions or more help. Using this approach, teachers and designers of learning environments may be more aggressive in raising student involvement by means of more focused approaches. These results highlight the necessity of a data-driven strategy to increase the efficacy of online learning as well as provide insightful analysis for the creation of more flexible and sensitive educational technology suited for student requirements.

articleTitle: Effective Alzheimer’s Stage Classification Using Transfer Learning Based on MRI Images
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Alzheimer’s disease (AD) is a progressive neurodegenerative disorder and the most prevalent cause of dementia, significantly impacting cognitive functions and daily activities. Accurate and timely classification of AD stages is of paramount importance for the effective treatment and management of the disease. The aim of this research is to employ transfer learning in a convolutional neural network (CNN) to classify the stages of AD using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) brain images, building on the aforementioned foundational principles. The CNN model employed in this study is MobileNetV3-Small, which has been trained on a comprehensive dataset of labeled MRI scans with the objective of accurately distinguishing the various stages of AD. The dataset, referred to as the “Augmented Alzheimer MRI Dataset,” comprises $\mathbf{3 3, 9 8 4}$ augmented and $\mathbf{6, 4 0 0}$ original MRI images, which have been categorized into four stages: Very Mild Demented, Moderate Demented, Mild Demented, and NonDemented. The methodology comprises three principal stages: data preparation, model training, and model evaluation. A systematic assessment of various hyperparameters, including split ratio, learning rate, batch size, and dropout rate, was conducted to optimize model performance. The results demonstrate that fine-tuning the model significantly enhances classification accuracy, achieving a maximum accuracy of $\mathbf{9 6 \%}$ compared to $\mathbf{7 2 \%}$ without fine-tuning. A smaller learning rate was found to improve performance metrics by preventing the model from converging to local minima. These findings highlight the potential of transfer learning and hyperparameter optimization in developing robust models for the early detection and classification of AD, contributing to better patient outcomes and advancing the field of medical image analysis.

articleTitle: Empowering Software Engineering Students: The Role of Gamification in Promoting Learning Independence
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: The role of learning media greatly supports the learning process, increasing motivation and interest in the process. Learning media can also be a place to improve competence optimally through bootcamp training menus and the like with more specific training objectives. The main objective of this study is to develop a gamification-based website to enhance students’ preparedness for their Final Competency Test by tackling challenges in comprehending programming absent practical experience. The learning method implemented in this website is case-based learning that integrates dynamic coding activities. The research method uses the Plomp approach with 3 main stages, namely preliminary research, prototyping, and assessment stage. The trial of the gamification website began with media and content validation followed by small group testing and large group testing. Validation by media and material experts led to the execution of small group trials (95.7%) and large group trials (91.7%), producing exceptionally positive outcomes. The results of the small group test with 12 respondents produced a very suitable value with a score of 95.7 and the large group test with 27 respondents produced a score of $\mathbf{9 1. 7 \%}$ with very suitable criteria. This indicates that the web-based platform is highly viable for assisting vocational students in acquiring software development skills, enhancing their preparedness for practical IT positions such as software developers and system analysts. Subsequent study involved the incorporation of gamification, such as computer-supported collaborative learning.

articleTitle: Indonesia Traffic Sign Recognition Using a One-Stage Detector YOLOv8
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Traffic is a key element in the transportation system. However, the increase in road accidents, which can be attributed to people’s lack of knowledge about traffic, is a growing concern. The primary solution to address this problem is to enhance traffic knowledge. The application of artificial intelligence, particularly object detection methods using detector-based deep learning, has proven efficient in real-time object detection. In this research, object recognition is performed using YOLOv8 (You Only Look Once). These models are trained and tested for their performance in detecting traffic signs in Indonesia. The results show that the mAP 50 and mAP $\mathbf{5 0 - 9 5}$ values were $\mathbf{9 9. 5 0 \%}$ and $\mathbf{9 9. 0 1 \%}$, respectively, for the YOLOv8 model. This demonstrates that YOLOv8 is the best-performing model for traffic sign detection in Indonesia.

articleTitle: Comparative Analysis of Multi-Face Detection Methods in Classroom Environments: Haar Cascade, MTCNN, YOLOFace, and RetinaFace
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Face detection in educational environments is vital for applications such as automated attendance systems, behavior analysis, and personalized learning tools. This study conducted a comprehensive comparative analysis of four advanced face detection algorithms—Haar Cascade, MTCNN, YOLOFace, and RetinaFace—using a dataset of real classroom images. The analysis addresses the unique challenges of classroom settings, including variable lighting, occlusions, and diverse student orientations. Metrics such as precision, recall, F1-score, and inference time were evaluated. YOLOFace and RetinaFace demonstrated superior performance, with YOLOFace achieving perfect precision, recall, and F1-score in most scenarios. RetinaFace also demonstrated high precision and recall, though its inference times were longer, up to 12.73 seconds. MTCNN exhibited high precision, up to 1.00, and recall, up to 0.97, but had higher inference times and occasionally missed some faces. Haar Cascade, while efficient with the shortest inference times, down to 0.54 seconds, displayed lower precision of 0.89 and recall of 0.25, resulting in a higher rate of missed detections. These findings emphasize the importance of selecting appropriate face detection models that address the specific challenges of educational environments to enhance the effectiveness of digital classroom applications.

articleTitle: Adapting the Scrum Framework for Agile Project Management: Case Study of a SISINTA Thesis Management Platform
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: The swift advancement of information technology has necessitated that educational institutions incorporate technological solutions into their administrative and instructional functions. One such solution is the integration of a thesis management system. Additionally, SISINTA, an all-inclusive web-based platform, was implemented to enhance the management of dissertation projects in educational institutions. The agile Scrum Software Development Life Cycle (SDLC) technique was used in the development of SISINTA. This methodology encourages flexibility, adaptability, and continual improvement based on real-time user feedback. Through the use of iterative sprints, SISINTA is always developing and adding new features to better meet the unique requirements of its consumers. Real-time thesis progress tracking, centralized document management, and collaboration tools that improve stakeholder contact are some of SISINTA’s key features. This study compares and contrasts SISINTA with other web-based thesis management systems, most of which emphasize cost-effectiveness or development driven by user feedback. Because of its powerful real-time monitoring and centralised management features, SISINTA stands out and works especially well in academic settings where supervision, tracking, and collaboration are essential. The results reveal that SISINTA considerably enhances the organisation, oversight and general efficiency of the thesis management process, making it a good solution for schools wishing to streamline their thesis processes. SISINTA maintains its high degree of adaptability and responsiveness by putting Agile Scrum concepts to use, making sure that it keeps up with the changing needs of instructors and students.

articleTitle: Desaign of a Portable Type Biogas Reactor From Wasted Food With The Addition of a Type Of Potassium Hydroxide Catalyst
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Biogas is one of the renewable energies produced by the the wasted powder. Powder is a waste from wood harvesting. fermentation process of organic materials derived from vegetable powder can accelerate the process of biogas fermentation, so that garbage. This study serves to measure and monitor the conditions decomposed powder is more easily processed by methanogenesis inside the biogas reactor. Four variations were performed, each bacteria [5]. Digesters are containers used to compose organic involving a substrate of 75 kilos of food residue and 75 kilograms of materials and produce biogas. water. In the first variation, 0.5 kg of potassium hydroxide was used as a catalyst, the second variation used 1 kg, the third variation 0.5 kg, and the fourth variation 1 kg. In this grinding used the batch method by inserting the entire substrate and catalyst at a time. The results show that the second variation produces the highest methane concentration of 63,782,235 ppm. The average gas temperature in the digester is 32°C. The rest of the food is in the beetle first and it’s hand-mounted three times a day. Biogas of the first and second variants are flammable, thus promising as a sustainable energy source. The study highlighted the importance of optimizing biogas production from food residue using different catalysts, and the addition of 1 kg of potassium hydroxide proved most effective in increasing methane production. Keywords— component, formatting, style, styling, insert

articleTitle: Machine Learning for Predictive Maintenance: A Literature Review
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Purpose: The advancement of Industry 4.0 has driven the adoption of predictive maintenance as a strategic step in optimizing equipment performance. Today, machine learning plays a key role in predicting potential equipment failures to minimize equipment downtime. However, assessing the accuracy of the predictive maintenance model presents a challenge for researchers in creating a reliable predictive maintenance model. Therefore, this review specifically focuses on the evaluation of the outputs of various related literatures. Design/methodology/approach: The approach used in making this review focuses on exploring the method of developing a predictive maintenance model with machine learning algorithms. This search is also carried out with the help of special software to search the literature database and screen the suitability of the research results, which is the main purpose of this literature review. Findings: Predictive maintenance models with machine learning algorithms such as support vector machines and random forests, including their integration with time-series classification and AdaBoost, demonstrate the ability of real-time abnormality prediction and equipment failure classification, as well as improve operational efficiency and resource optimization with high stability on complex data. Originality value: The results of this literature review are expected to be a guide for researchers and practitioners in exploring and validating ML algorithms to develop predictive maintenance models of equipment that can be accessed in real-time.

articleTitle: Brainwave Monitoring in Epileptic Pediatric Patient using MSAR-Normal, MSAR-Azzalini, and MSARExponential Power
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: This study aims to model brain wave data in children with special needs, specifically focusing on epilepsy, using the Markov Switching Autoregressive (MSAR) model. Given the substantial prevalence of children suffering from epilepsy in Indonesia, the implementation of precise interventions and monitoring is critical to fostering their cognitive and psychological well-being. Electroencephalograph (EEG) data were acquired from the Airlangga University Hospital, specifically focusing on the temporal region at the T3Cz channel. The MSAR-Normal model was selected for its capacity to effectively modeling the shifts in pattern dynamics and temporal dependencies. In nonlinear condition, challenges were encountered in satisfying the residual white noise assumption. The Bayesian approach was employed, to address these challenges by comparing the performance of the added distributions, Azzalini and Exponential Power (EP), into the MSAR model which are then called MSAR-Azzalini and MSAR-EP. The performance of this approach is evaluated against MSAR-Normal. The findings indicate that the MS(2)AR(1) model, particularly when utilizing the MSAR-EP, best represents the T3-Cz Channel. It achieves the AIC value of -1096.9, lower than the MSAR-Normal and MSAR-Azzalini model of 21813.2 and 20915.56. Furthermore, highly effective in detecting abnormal waves before and during seizures, and provides accurate personalized treatments.

articleTitle: A Design and Implementation of Water Heater Model Plant with Temperature Estimation Model for IOT Studies
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: This study presents the development of an Internet of Things (IoT) system for a water heater model, focusing on enhancing reliability during sensor malfunctions that could disrupt operations. Using the SEMAR IoT platform, the system efficiently collects and analyzes data, while the integration of the Holt-Winter algorithm ensures accurate temperature estimates, even with unreliable or missing sensor data. The algorithm successfully auto-calibrates sensors, predicts temperature at specific time intervals based on real sensor behavior, and fills in missing data during sensor failures. Tests show strong correlations between estimated and actual temperatures, allowing uninterrupted operation. This solution offers a flexible, cost-effective alternative to traditional redundancy, ensuring system reliability during sensor failures. Future research will explore alternative predictive models and conduct real-world testing to validate the system’s resilience under complex conditions.

articleTitle: Identification of Drug Dependence Types Using Case-Based Reasoning Expert System with K-Nearest Neighbour
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Drugs are a serious concern in developing countries, including Indonesia. Drug users, who are increasing every year, are a global problem that must be considered, not only by the government but also by the community. This increase is partly due to the ignorance of drug users about the type of drug dependence on themselves, making it difficult to cure themselves. Identification of dependence is very necessary. Therefore, this study uses the Case-Based Reasoning (CBR) method based on an expert system with K-Nearest Neighbor (KNN) to classify types of drug dependence. Types of drug dependence are based on the class of substances, namely Stimulants, Opioids (narcotics), Depressants, and Hallucinogens. The research data uses medical record data of drug users from 2018 to 2020. The results of the CBR method calculation with K-NN using 72 old case data and 30 new case data with confusion matrix testing obtained good accuracy results based on accuracy values of $\mathbf{8 1 \%} \%, \mathbf{7 6 \%}$ for precision, and $\mathbf{1 0 0 \%}$ for recall. From the test results, it can be seen that the CBR expert system with K-NN can identify types of drug dependence with a high level of accuracy.

articleTitle: Privacy at Risk: An Investigation of Data Collection Practices and Tracking Scripts on Government Websites in Java
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: The widespread use of the Internet has led users to frequently and unknowingly share personal information. This research conducted an analysis of the data typically collected and its impact on user privacy, as well as the current privacy policies and their contents. Numerous methods for analyzing privacy can be employed to complete this research. For instance, OpenWPM is one such method that involves gathering data on Internet user behavior by configuring the target URL. OpenWPM provides various options including cookie data collection and HTTP headers. It is also possible to manually analyze privacy. In this research, we conducted a privacy analysis of $\mathbf{1 2 5}$ government websites in Java (six provinces). Of these, 1,576 out of 3,492 (45%) websites had third-party tracking scripts and 955 out of 1,576 (65%) had cookies available in the third-party tracking scripts. All government websites in Java, except for Jakarta, were flagged as malicious by VirusTotal. Furthermore, none of the main domains of government websites had privacy policies and cookie availability was accepted.

articleTitle: Measurement of Information Security Awareness Level On Using Free Wi-Fi In Coffee Shop
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: The development of IT has increased the utilization of information and communication technology and the need for people to use Internet data. More social interactions are done virtually, making the internet network a primary need in the 21st-century era. Free Wi-Fi services have become a common facility in many places, including coffee shops, facilitating people’s activities in accessing information. However, using Wi-Fi networks in public places also risks personal data security, especially when information leakage occurs. Information leakage can lead to misuse of personal data. While raising awareness about protecting personal data is important, public awareness about data security is still low. This study aims to measure information security awareness levels regarding using free $\mathrm{Wi}-\mathrm{Fi}$ in coffee shops. The measurement awareness level of data security, researchers used the HAIS-Q (Human Aspects of Information Security Questionnaire) method, which includes three dimensions: knowledge, attitudes, and behaviour (KAB), which were further developed with seven indicators: password management, email use, internet use, social media use, mobile use, information handling, and incident reporting. The results of this study are that the level of information security awareness of free Wi-Fi users in coffee shops is classified as moderate, with an average condition of $74.55 \%$. It was found that the dimensions of knowledge, attitudes, and behaviour related to information security were still in the moderate category. From the regression analysis that has been carried out, a significant relationship was found between the variables used in measuring the level of security awareness of privacy data for free Wi-Fi users in coffee shops.

articleTitle: Virtual Focus: How Avatar and No-Instructor Video Lectures Enhance Learning Gain and Visual Attention
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: This study investigates the impact of different types of instructor presence on learning outcomes and visual attention in video-based learning. Using eye-tracking technology and pre-and post-tests, we evaluated three instructional conditions: the absence of an instructor, the physical presence of an instructor, and the instructor’s virtual presence as an avatar. The results reveal that the physical presence of an instructor tends to divide learners’ attention, often leading to lower learning outcomes compared to the avatar or no instructor conditions. In contrast, the virtual instructor as an avatar helps maintain learner focus on the educational content, resulting in higher learning gains, further suggesting that reducing distractions enhances learning. Additionally, an analysis of the relation between slide type, hotspot count, and learning gain revealed that image-centric slides with fewer hotspots yielded the highest learning gains. This research highlights the importance of optimising instructor presence in video-based learning materials to improve learning outcomes, and it provides practical insights for instructional design in distance learning environments.

articleTitle: SmartCourse: An Intelligent Recommender System for Course Offerings and Student Course Advising
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)

authors.preferredName: Jessie Richie N. De Los Santos

abstract: Recommender systems improve decision-making and streamline procedures, significantly changing multiple sectors, including education. Biliran Province State University’s (BiPSU) manual processes to advise courses for students and manage course offerings cause errors, inefficiencies, and conflicts with standard regulations. This study introduces SmartCourse, an intelligent system that utilizes binary logistic regression to predict student outcomes and optimize course offerings for upcoming semesters. The SmartCourse has four main phases to generate appropriate course offerings, including head count, student eligibility, course priority, and new class phases. By automating these processes, the system significantly improves the efficiency of course advising, ensuring that students are recommended courses based on prioritization and eligibility criteria. Quantitative research, involving surveys and interviews was conducted to collect data from BiPSU students, program chairs, and STCS professors to design and assess the system. The assessment, based on ISO 25010 Software Quality Standards, revealed high user satisfaction with the system’s usability (4.24/5), functional appropriateness (4.38/5), and performance efficiency ($4.41 / 5$). The results showed that users were very satisfied with SmartCourse. It effectively manages course offerings and course advising, improving accuracy and efficiency and saving time and resources. Likewise, it contributes significantly to the educational technology field by providing a solid solution to improve the decision-making processes in advising courses and course offerings. While SmartCourse is tailored for BiPSU, its flexible architecture allows for adaption in various institutional settings. Further research will focus on expanding the system to handle cross-program offerings and advising across departments, as well as evaluate the system’s long-term impact on student success, academic outcomes, and institutional efficiency.

articleTitle: Leveraging Fine-Tuned YOLOv8 with Transfer Learning for Peritoneal Carcinomatosis Detection
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Peritoneal Carcinomatosis (PC) is a severe disease where cancer spreads to the peritoneal lining, and patients with this condition have a high risk of mortality. Early detection of this disease is crucial for improving patient survival chances. This study utilizes the YOLOv8 model to detect PC using a dataset of 4,197 laparoscopy images. YOLOv8 was chosen for its capability in fast and accurate object detection. The model training process involves using pretrained weights for fine-tuning to enhance detection performance. Model hyperparameters were optimized, and data augmentation was applied to improve model generalization. Experimental results show that the YOLOv8m model performs the best, with a mean Average Precision (mAP50) of 0.871, precision of 0.893, recall of 0.785, and an F1 score of 0.84. The use of fine-tuned pre-trained weights on the PC dataset shows a significant improvement in results compared to models trained without pre-trained weights.

articleTitle: Clickbait in the Era of Information Technology: Evaluating Engagement Strategies and Ethical Journalism in Online Media
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: In the digital era, clickbait has become a common strategy among online media to attract attention and increase audience engagement. This study aims to evaluate the balance between efforts to attract attention through clickbait and efforts to maintain journalistic ethical standards in online media. This case study used short videos uploaded by YouTube Tribun Timur during July 2023. The research population consisted of 442 videos, with a sample taken using probability sampling techniques, resulting in 82 videos for analysis. This research used a quantitative approach with a content analysis method. To ensure data validity, this study applied content validity and face validity. Data reliability was tested using the Holsti method, involving two independent coders to ensure consistency of judgment. The results showed that teasing clickbait was the most dominantly used, followed by ambiguous and inflammatory, while Tribun Timur did not use graphics, bait and switch, or false clickbait. Excessive use of clickbait tends to decrease audience trust and damage the media’s reputation. This research confirms that while clickbait can increase audience engagement in the short term, its long-term impact on journalistic integrity and audience trust is detrimental. Media outlets, including Tribun Timur, should commit to prioritizing journalistic ethics and using technology to create a more honest and transparent media environment.

articleTitle: Multi-GPU Implementation of Convolutional Neural Networks for Vegetable and Fruit Image Recognition
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: This study explores the implementation of Convolutional Neural Networks (CNNs) using multiple Graphics Processing Units (GPUs) for image recognition tasks, specifically focusing on classifying vegetables and fruits. The primary objective is to evaluate the impact of parallel processing on model training time and accuracy. By distributing the computational workload across multiple GPUs, we aimed to reduce training duration while maintaining or improving model accuracy. Our experimental results show that the multi-GPU setup achieved superior accuracy, with validation accuracy reaching 95.7%, compared to $\mathbf{9 0. 2 \%}$ on a single GPU. However, the multi-GPU setup required 242.23 seconds for training, slightly longer than the 233.64 seconds needed by the single GPU due to synchronization overhead. This paper provides insights into the practical deployment of multi-GPU systems for CNN-based image recognition and discusses the implications of our findings for optimizing large-scale deep learning tasks in real-world applications.

articleTitle: Application of Students Graduation Prediction Model Using Decision Tree C4.5 Algorithm and Synthetic Minority Oversampling Technique (SMOTE)
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: An important achievement for students and higher education institutions is timely graduation. Unfortunately, a large number of students fail to graduate on time, which can have a negative impact on the accreditation of higher education institutions. Academic authorities can improve the timely graduation rate by developing policies and regulations with the help of student graduation prediction. Using academic data, data mining is an efficient way to predict graduation. Consequently, the Decision Tree C4.5 approach is used in this study to predict student graduation. This study also uses the SMOTE oversampling technique to address class imbalance in minority data and the mean method to manage missing variables. According to the findings, the first-semester grade point average (GPA) has the greatest impact on graduation. Overall GPA, GPA from the fourth semester, and GPA from the second semester are additional significant factors. An accuracy of ${8 4. 4 \%}$, precision of ${8 8. 8 \%}$, recall of ${8 3. 4 \%}$, and F1 score of 0.852 with N value of $100 \%$ for SMOTE were obtained through model testing using 5-Fold Cross Validation with SMOTE. The results of the model without SMOTE are $81.6\%$ accuracy, $87\%$ precision, ${8 4. 8 \%}$ recall, and an ${F 1}$ score of ${0. 8 5 0}$. Furthermore, with ${8 2. 8 \%}$ accuracy, the highest parameter values for tree depth are 5 and 10.

articleTitle: Enhancing Learning Interest in Basic Programming for First-Year Vocational Students through Website-Based Gamified Problem-Based Learning
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Learning basic programming is important as a programming guide or foundation that provides the basics of logic in creating programs. Some students expressed a lack of interest in learning the basics of software and game development. Less flexible and less attractive teaching media can reduce student interest in learning. Therefore, researchers developed learning media using gamification with a website-based problem-based learning model. This study aims to determine the performance and measure the feasibility and effectiveness of website learning media with gamification using the problem-based learning model in basic software development and game subjects. This research was conducted using the Borg & Gall research and development model consisting of data collection, planning, initial product development, initial product testing and revision, small-scale trials and revision, and large-scale trials. This research and development resulted in a website learning media product with gamification using the Problem-Based Learning model that can be accessed online which obtained a media expert validation value of $\mathbf{9 2. 6 1 \%}$ or very feasible, the acquisition of a material expert validation value of 92.50% or very feasible, the acquisition of a small-scale trial value of 88.21% or very feasible, then the acquisition of a large-scale trial value of $\mathbf{9 0. 0 0 \%}$ or very feasible, and an increase in learning interest obtained a gain value of 0.43 after using website learning media with gamification using the problem based learning model, from a percentage of $\mathbf{7 0. 3 2 \%}$ to $\mathbf{8 3. 0 6 \%}$ with a moderate increase category.

articleTitle: Examining Gen-Z Intention to Participate in Deposit Refund Systems: A Convergent Mixed-Method Study in Indonesia
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: The rising environmental challenges in waste management have prompted an urgent need for effective recycling initiatives. This study investigates the intention of Generation Z (Gen-Z) in Indonesia to participate in a Deposit Refund System (DRS), a system aimed at promoting recycling behaviors. Using a convergent mixed-method approach, quantitative data from 228 respondents were analyzed via Partial Least Squares Structural Equation Modeling (PLS-SEM) to assess relationships between intention, distrust, environmental concern, and behavioral intention. Qualitative data analysis, employing vector embedding and k-means clustering, revealed key patterns and themes in Gen-Z’s attitudes. Integration of qualitative and quantitative results through PLS-SEM provided a comprehensive understanding of Gen-Z motivations towards environmental sustainability. The results show that environmental concern positively impacts behavioral intention, while distrust was found to be statistically insignificant. This study offers practical and academic insights for policymakers to design more effective DRS initiatives. Future research could explore the long-term behavioral shifts resulting from DRS participation and the role of digital platforms in enhancing engagement.

articleTitle: Learning Analytics on YouTube Video Learning Content Using Clustering Method
publicationTitle: 2024 Seventh International Conference on Vocational Education and Electrical Engineering (ICVEE)
abstract: Learning resources are one of the important things that support student learning. Learning resources could be used as an amplification outside the class to the learning material delivered by the teacher.
